  WHY: That condition is never true in this context, so the skip feature cannot run at all; severity remains critical as reported.

  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2]
  PROBLEM: The post-commit dispatch guard suppresses `workflow_dispatch` retrigger for normal autofix commits.
  WHY: With the gate skip also non-functional, suppressing the retrigger can stop the autofix loop before another verification run occurs.

  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: The gate job continues to evaluate the self-triggered skip logic even when `SHOULD_RUN` has already been set to false by a preceding check.
  WHY: The reviewer says this causes redundant API calls and can conflate skip reasons when `SHOULD_RUN` was already false.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:112 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: The gate job attempts to fetch PR state via `gh api` even when `SHOULD_RUN` has already been set to false due to a non-numeric `PR_NUMBER`.
  WHY: The reviewer says the shell continues into the API call path, which can produce avoidable errors and obscure the original skip reason.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:179-212 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Self-triggered skip logic checks for `EVENT_NAME == 'pull_request'`, but this is a reusable workflow called via `workflow_call`, so `EVENT_NAME` is always `workflow_call`.
  WHY: The skip logic will never execute because the condition `[ "${EVENT_NAME}" = "pull_request" ]` is always false in a reusable workflow.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3839-3870 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Post-commit dispatch guard suppresses `workflow_dispatch` retrigger for normal autofix commits. Combined with (non-working) gate skip, this could break the autofix loop entirely.
  WHY: After an autofix commit, no verification run occurs (dispatch is suppressed, and synchronize run would be skipped if gate worked). The autofix process stops even if issues remain unfixed.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:194 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: TSV parsing with `cut -f1` is fragile if commit subject contains tab characters.
  WHY: If commit subject contains a tab, `cut -f1` only extracts text before the tab, causing incorrect parsing of the commit message line.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:201-202 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: GitHub login comparison is case-sensitive, but GitHub logins are case-insensitive.
  WHY: If `AUTOFIX_BOT_LOGIN` uses different casing than the actual GitHub login (e.g., `Codex` vs `codex`), legitimate bot commits won't be skipped.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:179-212 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The gate step continues execution after setting `SHOULD_RUN=false` for non-numeric PR numbers.
  WHY: The reviewer says the script still reaches later logic after the non-numeric check, though it does not cause functional issues.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:180 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The gate job continues to evaluate the self-triggered skip logic even when SHOULD_RUN has already been set to false by a preceding check.
  WHY: This results in redundant API calls and potentially overwrites or conflates skip reasons when SHOULD_RUN was already false due to a draft PR, [skip ai] marker, or invalid PR number.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:195 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Parsing the head_meta TSV output with 'cut -f1' is fragile because valid commit subjects can contain tab characters.
  WHY: A tab character in the commit subject will truncate the head_msg_line, potentially causes the subject prefix check ("[ai-autofix]"*) to fail or produces inaccurate audit logs, leading to missed skips or difficult-to-debug logging.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:112 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The gate job attempts to fetch the PR state via 'gh api' even when SHOULD_RUN has already been set to false due to a non-numeric PR_NUMBER.
  WHY: The shell script continues to the 'else' block and attempts 'gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}"'. If PR_NUMBER is non-numeric, the API call will fail (typically with a 404 or 422), cluttering the logs with errors and potentially masking the original "invalid_pr_number" skip reason if the API failure path behaves unexpectedly.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3858 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The comment indicates that the mirror guard relies on DID_COMMIT and CONFLICT_RESOLVED flags, but the check on line 3861 doesn't verify if these variables are actually set or if they are exported from the environment.
  WHY: If the previous steps in the job fail to export DID_COMMIT or CONFLICT_RESOLVED (or if they are unset due to a shell environment scope issue), the '[-n "${DID_COMMIT}"]' check might fail or behave inconsistently. While line 3862 uses defaults ("${DID_COMMIT:-false}"), line 3863 uses "${CONFLICT_RESOLVED:-false}". If CONFLICT_RESOLVED is missing, it defaults to false, which satisfies the '!= "true"' condition, potentially causing a skip when it shouldn't if the previous state was lost.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:201-202 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The comparison uses bash `=` operator which is case-sensitive:
  WHY: GitHub usernames are case-insensitive. If a user configures `AUTOFIX_BOT_LOGIN=Codex` (with capital C) while the actual bot pushes as `codex`, the skip will fail to recognize its own commits.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:194 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The code parses TSV output using `cut -f1`:
  WHY: While the commit message is split via `split("\n")[0]` in jq to get only the first line, if the commit subject itself contains tab characters, `cut -f1` would truncate at the first tab, causing the logged `head_msg_line` to be incomplete/incorrect for audit purposes.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:108-119 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When PR_NUMBER is numeric but the PR state API call succeeds but returns empty state, the code at lines 122-133 sets SHOULD_RUN="false" with skip_reason="pr_state_unknown".
  WHY: There is a slight inefficiency in that the API call is made before knowing whether `pr_state` will be empty, but this is likely acceptable since the PR state is needed for other checks.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:178-212 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Self-triggered skip logic executes GitHub API call even when SHOULD_RUN already set to false by earlier gates
  WHY: When PR_NUMBER is invalid, PR is closed/draft, or contains skip markers, SHOULD_RUN becomes "false" but the self-triggered skip block (lines 178+) still runs its gh api call and processes the result. This wastes API calls unnecessarily.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:194 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: TSV parsing with `cut -f1` breaks if commit subject contains tab characters
  WHY: The jq query uses `@tsv` format which escapes tabs in the commit message as `\t`. When `cut -f1` processes this, a tab in the original commit subject would create extra fields, causing head_msg_line to contain only the portion before the first tab instead of the full subject line. The `[ai-autofix]` prefix check may still work if the tab appears after the prefix, but prefix detection would fail if the tab is within `[ai-autofix]`.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:201-202 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: GitHub login comparison is case-sensitive but GitHub logins are case-insensitive
  WHY: If a user sets AUTOFIX_BOT_LOGIN="Codex" or "CODEX" but the actual GitHub API returns "codex", the comparison `[ "${head_author_login}" = "${bot_login}" ]` fails and the skip doesn't trigger.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:104-106 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: PR state API call proceeds even after invalid PR number sets SHOULD_RUN=false
  WHY: The reviewer later notes this appears incorrect because the API call is inside the `else` block that only executes for valid numeric PR numbers.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:194-196 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The commit metadata is formatted as TSV using jq's @tsv, but the subject line may contain tab characters.
  WHY: Using `cut -f1/2/3` to extract fields will mis-parse if the subject contains a tab, misaligning author/committer fields and truncating the subject; this can cause the `[ai-autofix]` prefix check to fail or produce incorrect author/committer values.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:201-202 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: GitHub login comparison is case-sensitive (`[ "${head_author_login}" = "${bot_login}" ]`). GitHub logins are case-insensitive, so if `AUTOFIX_BOT_LOGIN` uses different casing than the actual login (e.g., "Codex" vs "codex"), the identity guard fails and the skip does not occur.
  WHY: Legitimate bot commits are not skipped, causing redundant reviewer/editor cycles and extra LLM spend.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
